Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and may Allah's blessings and peace be upon our Prophet Muhammad, and upon his family and companions, and those who follow them in goodness until the Day of Judgment.

To proceed: this is the seventy-third of the "Open Door" sessions, which take place every Thursday of the week. This Thursday is the tenth of Rabi' al-Thani in the year one thousand four hundred and fifteen (AH). In it we discuss the beginning of Surah ash-Shams, where Allah, may He be blessed and exalted, says: ﴿By the sun and its brightness, (1) And the moon when it follows it, (2) And the day when it displays it, (3) And the night when it covers it, (4) And the heaven and He who built it, (5) And the earth and He who spread it, (6) And a soul and He who proportioned it﴾ [ash-Shams 1–7], and so on to the end.

As for the basmalah (the opening "In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate"), we will not repeat the discussion of it, since it is well known and recurs often. Instead, we begin with the verses.

Regarding the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿وَالشَّمْسِ وَضُحَاهَا﴾ [By the sun and its brightness]: Allah swears by the sun and its brightness, which is its light, because of what this contains of great signs that indicate the perfection of Allah's power, the perfection of His knowledge and His mercy, the Exalted. Indeed, in this sun there are signs that some people do not grasp. Let me give you an example: when the sun rises, how much electrical energy does it save the world? It saves thousands of millions, because people do without that energy by means of it. And how much heat does the earth receive from it, for the ripening of fruits and the goodness of trees, that only Allah, Mighty and Majestic, knows. And it brings many benefits to the earth that I cannot enumerate, because most of them relate to astronomy (ʿilm al-falak), earth science, and geology, and I cannot list them; but they are among the great signs of Allah.

Surah 91, verse 2:

﴿By the moon when it follows it﴾. It has been said: when it follows it in its course; and it has been said: when it follows it in giving light. Since the verse can bear both of these meanings, the rule in the science of tafsir (the explanation of the Qur'an) is that when a verse can bear two meanings, both must be taken, because taking both meanings together gives the meaning greater scope.

So we say: [it follows it] in its course, because the moon falls back a little each day relative to the sun. So when you see it at the beginning of the month close to it in the west (al-maghrib), by the middle of the month it is at its farthest from it in the east (al-mashriq), since it falls back each day. Or: [it follows it] in giving light, because when the sun sets the light of the moon appears, especially in the second quarter up to the end of the third quarter, when the moonlight is clear and evident. That is, when seven days have passed and seven days remain, the light is weak; from the passing of seven days until seven days remain, the light is strong, whereas in the first seven days and the last seven days it is weak. In any case, the moon's light only appears after the sun's light has gone, as is apparent. So Allah swears by the sun because it is the sign of the day, and by the moon because it is the sign of the night.

﴿And by the moon when it follows it (2), and by the day when it reveals it (3), and by the night when it covers it.﴾

Antithesis (tadad): the day, when it reveals the earth, makes it clear, manifests it, and brings it into view, because it is a day by which things become distinct and evident.

And the night when it covers it (the sun). It covers the earth until it becomes like a cloak spread over something of things, and this becomes clear when the sun sets while you are in an airplane. When the sun sets while you are in the airplane, you find that the earth beneath you is dark, because you are now still seeing the sun due to your height, but the earth beneath you, where the sun has set upon it, you find it dark, as if it were covered with a black cloak. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿And the night when it covers it﴾.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 91, verse 5:

﴿By the sky and He who built it﴾ (5) ﴿and by the earth﴾. The sky and the earth are opposites (mutaqabilat).

﴿By the sky and He who built it﴾ (5) ﴿and by the earth and He who spread it out﴾ (6) ﴿and by the soul and He who proportioned it﴾.

﴿By the sky and He who built it﴾. The commentators said: here "ma" (what) is a verbal-noun particle (ma masdariyya), meaning: "by the sky and its building"; because the sky is great in its height, its vastness, its strength, and other things which are among the signs of Allah in it. Likewise, its construction is a firm construction, as Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿You will not see in the creation of the Most Merciful any imbalance. So return your sight; do you see any flaw? (3) Then return your sight twice; your sight will return to you humbled while it is fatigued﴾ [al-Mulk: 3-4].

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 91, verse 6:

﴿And the earth and He who spread it out﴾ [ash-Shams: 6]. He means: the earth and He who made it level, so that it is even, and so that it is neither too soft nor too hard and firm, but suitable for creation according to what their needs require. This is among the blessings of Allah, glorified and exalted be He, upon His servants, that He made the earth level for them and placed it between softness and roughness, except in some places; but this little does not make a ruling over the much.

﴿By the soul and He who proportioned it﴾. Here, "nafs" (soul), although singular, is meant in a general sense: every soul.

﴿And He who proportioned it﴾ means He proportioned it in creation (khilqah) and proportioned it in natural disposition (fitrah). He proportioned it in creation by creating everything in the form that suits it and suits its condition. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Our Lord is He who gave everything its form, then guided it﴾ [Ta-Ha 50], meaning: He gave it the form suited to it, and then guided it to its benefits.

Likewise, He proportioned it in fitrah, especially mankind, for Allah the Exalted made their fitrah to be sincere devotion (ikhlas) and monotheism (tawhid). As He the Exalted said: ﴿So direct your face toward the religion, inclining to truth. [Adhere to] the fitrah of Allah upon which He created mankind﴾ [al-Rum 30].

**Ibn 'Uthaymin:** *Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Karim*, on Surah 91, verse 8:

﴿So He inspired it [with knowledge of] its wickedness and its righteousness.﴾ [al-Shams 8] Who is the one who inspires? Allah, Mighty and Majestic. He inspired these souls.

﴿So He inspired it [with knowledge of] its wickedness and its righteousness.﴾ He mentioned wickedness (*fujur*) before righteousness (*taqwa*), even though taqwa is undoubtedly better. They said: this is out of consideration for the verse endings (*fawasil*).

﴿He inspired it [with knowledge of] its wickedness and its righteousness.﴾ What is *fujur*? We say: it is the opposite of taqwa, and taqwa is obedience to Allah. Therefore *fujur* is disobedience to Allah. Every disobedient person is a *fajir* (wicked person). Although in common usage *al-fajir* has been restricted to one who is not chaste, in the Shari'ah it encompasses everyone who departs from obedience to Allah, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Nay, indeed the record of the wicked is in Sijjin.﴾ [al-Mutaffifin 7] and the intended meaning there is the disbelievers.

As for ﴿and He inspired it with its taqwa﴾, meaning He inspired it with taqwa. Which of the two agrees with the *fitrah* (innate disposition): the second or the first?

* Students: The second.

* The Shaykh: The second, because *fujur* lies outside the *fitrah*. Yet Allah may inspire some souls with deviation because of their deviation, as He the Exalted says: ﴿So when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate.﴾ [al-Saff 5] Allah the Exalted does not wrong anyone, but whoever Allah knows does not want the truth, Allah causes his heart to deviate. We ask Allah for well-being.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 91, verse 9:

﴿Indeed, the one who purifies it has succeeded, (9) and the one who corrupts it has failed.﴾ [al-Shams: 9, 10]

﴿Indeed, he has succeeded﴾: i.e., he has attained what he sought and was saved from what he feared.

﴿Who purifies it﴾: i.e., who purifies his soul. The purification intended here is not the self-praise (tazkiyah) that is forbidden in His words: ﴿So do not claim your own purity﴾ [al-Najm: 32]. The purification meant here is that one purifies one's soul by cleansing it of polytheism and the taints of sins, until it remains pure, clean and immaculate.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 91, verse 10:

﴿And he has failed who instills it (with corruption).﴾ That is: whoever corrupts it (the soul) by casting it into ruin and into acts of disobedience. In reality, this requires asking Allah, glorified and exalted, to make a person firm in His obedience and in "the firm word." So, O my Muslim brother, always ask Allah for steadfastness, beneficial knowledge, and righteous action; for Allah, the Exalted, said in His Book: ﴿And when My servants ask you concerning Me, indeed I am near. I respond to the invocation of the supplicant when he calls upon Me. So let them respond to Me [by obedience] and believe in Me that they may be rightly guided.﴾ [al-Baqarah 186].

We ask Allah to make us and you among the rightly guided, righteous, and reformers.

Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and may Allah's peace and blessings be upon our Prophet Muhammad, and upon his family and companions, and those who follow them in goodness until the Day of Judgment.

To proceed: this is the seventy-fourth of the sessions held every Thursday, and this is the twenty-fourth Thursday of the month of Rabi' al-Thani in the year one thousand four hundred and fifteen (after the Hijrah). In this session we complete the tafsir of Surah (Wa-sh-Shams wa-Duhaha), where we reached the words of Allah, blessed and exalted: ﴿Thamud denied (their prophet) in their transgression, when the most wretched of them was sent forth﴾ [ash-Shams 11–12].

﴿Thamud denied﴾: Thamud is the name of a tribe, and their prophet was Salih, peace be upon him. Their dwellings in al-Hijr are well known to travelers. These people denied their prophet Salih. Their prophet Salih, peace be upon him, like the other prophets, called them to worship Allah alone, without partner, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him that there is no deity except Me, so worship Me﴾ [al-Anbya' 25]. He called them to worship Allah alone, without partner, and Allah the Exalted gave him a sign that testifies to his prophethood, namely the great she-camel, which drinks from the well one day and provides you with milk on the second day.

Some scholars have said that whenever a person came and gave her water in proportion, she gave him milk in proportion. But what appears from the Qur'an is otherwise, because of the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿For her is a share of drink, and for you is a share of a known day﴾ [ash-Shu'ara' 155]. So the she-camel drinks from the well on one day, then yields milk on the second day. But did this verse benefit them?

Listen to the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Thamud denied (their prophet) in their transgression﴾ [ash-Shams 11], i.e., in their rebellion and insolence, and the preposition bi- here indicates causation, meaning: because of their being transgressors, they denied the Messenger.

﴿When the most wretched of them was sent forth﴾ [ash-Shams 12]: this explains the transgression that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, mentioned, and that was when the most wretched of them was sent forth. ﴿Was sent forth﴾ means set out swiftly, and ﴿the most wretched of them﴾ means the most wretched of Thamud, i.e., the foremost of them in wretchedness—we seek refuge in Allah. He wanted to put an end to this she-camel. Then Salih said to them: ﴿The she-camel of Allah, and her drink﴾ [ash-Shams 13]. He said to them: ﴿The she-camel of Allah﴾, i.e., leave the she-camel of Allah alone, because of the Lord's saying in another verse: ﴿So leave her to feed on Allah's earth﴾ [al-A'raf 73], meaning: leave the she-camel, do not kill her, do not harm her in any way. But the outcome was the reverse.

Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and may Allah's peace and blessings be upon our Prophet Muhammad, and upon his family and companions, and those who follow them in goodness until the Day of Judgment.

But the outcome was the reverse.

﴿So they denied him﴾ [al-Shams 91:14]. That is, they denied Salih and said, "You are not a messenger." This is the case with all the messengers who were sent to their peoples: their peoples charge them with defects, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Likewise, no messenger came to those before them but they said, "A sorcerer or a madman!"﴾ [al-Dhariyat 51:52]. Every messenger was told this: "A sorcerer or a madman." It was also said of the Messenger (ﷺ) that he was a sorcerer, a liar, a madman, a poet, and a soothsayer. But do the evil titles that enemies give to the friends of Allah harm them?

The answer: they do not harm them. Rather, through them they gain greater elevation with Allah, the Exalted, and if they seek their reward from Allah, they are rewarded for it.

So He, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿So they denied him and hamstrung her﴾ [al-Shams 91:14]. That is, they hamstrung the she-camel in a way that brought about their destruction.

﴿Their Lord crushed them over their sin and leveled them﴾ [al-Shams 91:14]. ﴿Crushed them﴾ means He closed over them and destroyed them, as you say, "I dammamtu the well," meaning I closed the earth over it.

﴿Their Lord crushed them over their sin﴾ means because of their sins. This is because Allah, the Exalted, ﴿does not wrong people at all, but it is people who wrong themselves﴾ [Yunus 10:44]. Sins are therefore a cause of destruction, ruin, and corruption, as the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, indicates: ﴿Corruption has appeared on land and sea because of what the hands of people have earned, that He may let them taste part of what they have done, so that they might return﴾ [al-Rum 30:41]. Allah the Exalted also said: ﴿And when We intend to destroy a city, We command its affluent ones, but they defiantly commit wickedness therein; so the word is justified against it, and We destroy it with complete destruction﴾ [al-Isra 17:16]. And Allah the Exalted addressed the best of creation and the best generations, saying: ﴿When a disaster struck you, although you had inflicted twice as much, you said, "From where is this?" Say, "It is from yourselves"﴾ [Al 'Imran 3:165]. A person is afflicted with calamities because of himself. Therefore He said: ﴿Their Lord crushed them over their sin﴾, that is, because of their sin.

﴿And leveled them﴾ means He encompassed them all with destruction, so that not one of them remained, and they became lifeless in their homes, prostrate.

Almighty Allah says: ﴿And He does not fear its consequence﴾ [ash-Shams 15]. This means that Allah, exalted is He, does not fear the consequence of those whom He punished, nor does He fear their repercussions, because sovereignty belongs to Him and everything is in His hand. This is unlike other kings: if kings are victorious over others or punish others, you find them in fear, worrying that the tables may be turned against them. As for Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿He does not fear its consequence﴾, that is, He does not fear the outcome for those whom He punished, because He, glory be to Him and exalted is He, possesses all sovereignty and all praise belongs to Him. Glory be to Him and exalted is He, how great He is! And how majestic is His authority!
